messages:
alex: quick heads-up, after the kernel-selector v2 rollout to canary cluster we see host-side p99 tokenization+parse latency up ~18ms. rolling back on canary reduces it. anyone else see this?
maria: ugh, saw that too around 03:20 UTC. traced it to increased writev syscall counts from streaming layer, oddly.
chen: I profiled a few requests — host parse time moved from ~3ms -> ~12ms on long-stream cases (seq 512). KV cache hit-rate steady though. suspect batching heuristics + kernel switch changed chunk sizes.
tyler: can you paste perf script output? especially syscalls and small-write counts.
alex: pasted a short trace below. this is a single request p99 sample from canary:
```
syscalls: writev=84, sendmsg=12, recv=3
user_time_ms: 7.1
kernel_time_ms: 10.9
parse_ms: 9.8
tokenize_ms: 1.2
kv_lookup_ms: 0.6
kvcache_hit: true
batch_size: 1
chunk_bytes: 256,256,128,64
```
maria: writev count jump is suspicious — previous normal run had writev=6 for similar request. that many small chunks causes kernel overhead + Nagle-ish interactions on http2.
sam: also saw more small-socket-writes when kernel selection picks the new attention kernel (mem-bound path). it increases decode bursts and triggers smaller streaming flushes.
chen: hypothesis: kernel v2 changes token emission pacing (smaller emits), which our streaming framer treats as separate chunks; batching heuristics don't coalesce because batch_size=1 and an early flush policy triggers.
tyler: can we try 2 quick mitigations on canary: 1) change framer flush threshold to 512 bytes for a minute, 2) force kernel-selector to prefer legacy kernel for seq>256 and compare.
alex: i'm happy to flip the flush threshold. doing 1 now on canary. will report in 10m.
ops-bot: deploy: framer/flush-threshold set to 512 on cluster-canary by alex (@7902461370).
maria: also capturing tcpdump for a sample request to validate chunk coalescing.
chen: if that mitigates, longer-term fixes: update batching heuristic to consider kernel-emitted burstiness, and add a short coalescing timer (2ms) in the framer to combine tiny emits.
sam: +1 for coalescing timer. also recommend recording kernel-id in trace spans so routing + framer can be kernel-aware.
tyler: i'm going to run a microbenchmark that simulates kernel v2 emit pattern and measure writev counts with different framer configs. will post numbers.
alex: update: 10m in — p99 reduced from +18ms to +4ms after threshold bump. writev counts dropped from ~80->9 on sampled traces.
maria: sweet. that's a strong signal that it's chunking, not kvcache.
chen: next steps: (a) add kernel-id to spans, (b) add transient coalesce timer, (c) tweak batching heuristic to allow small auto-batch when kernel is bursty. i'll open a PR with perf tests.
sam: can you include a small test harness that emits 1000 requests with kernel v2 pattern? we should guard regressions.
alex: thanks all — creating follow-up issue and will hold kernel-selector rollout until we ship mitigations.
ops-bot: ticket created: INF-2742 "Host framer coalesce + kernel-aware batching" by alex
